title: Minimum Spanning Tree: Prim
contract: Return minimum total weight connecting every vertex of a connected undirected weighted graph; n ≥ 1. Return −1 when disconnected.
brute: boolean[] used=new boolean[n];used[0]=true;long total=0;for(int step=1;step<n;step++){int[] best=null;for(int[] edge:edges)if(used[edge[0]]!=used[edge[1]]&&(best==null||edge[2]<best[2]))best=edge;if(best==null)return -1;used[best[0]]=used[best[1]]=true;total+=best[2];emit("Scan all edges across the cut","edge",best,"total",total);}return total;
optimal: List<List<int[]>> g=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<n;i++)g.add(new ArrayList<>());for(int[] e:edges){g.get(e[0]).add(new int[]{e[1],e[2]});g.get(e[1]).add(new int[]{e[0],e[2]});}PriorityQueue<int[]> q=new PriorityQueue<>(Comparator.comparingInt(x->x[1]));q.add(new int[]{0,0});boolean[] used=new boolean[n];long total=0;int count=0;while(!q.isEmpty()){int[] edge=q.remove();int u=edge[0];if(used[u])continue;used[u]=true;count++;total+=edge[1];for(int[] next:g.get(u))if(!used[next[0]])q.add(next);emit("Choose the cheapest edge leaving the tree","vertex",u,"total",total,"visited",used);}return count==n?total:-1;
reasoning: The baseline repeatedly scans all edges to find the cheapest crossing from the current tree to an unvisited vertex.
The cut property permits adding a minimum crossing edge without excluding every minimum spanning tree.
A priority queue avoids rescanning all edges. Skip edges to visited vertices and check that all vertices were reached; MST is not the same as shortest-path distance from a source.
